newsitem.title: UK: LOW & BONAR SQUEEZED UP ON STOCK SHORTAGE.
newsitem.headline: LOW & BONAR SQUEEZED UP ON STOCK SHORTAGE.

text.p: Shares in UK plastics and packaging group Low & Bonar Plc rose over 7.5 percent on Tuesday in thin volume as buying interest in the shares exacerbated a shortage of the stock, dealers said.
Low & Bonar shares gained 19p to 267-1/2p by 1341 GMT in volume of 195,000 shares, making it the best performing stock amongst the top 350 UK companies.

"It's a classic squeeze," said one dealer. "It's one of these bombed-out FTSE 250 stocks that is back in favour after sterling's fall (in the foreign exchange markets). People try to buy it but there are no natural sellers at these lower levels, and the shares get squeezed higher."
One dealer suggested Low & Bonar's recent acquisition of Nuway Manufacturing from BTR Plc for 11 million stg had boosted sentiment towards the shares.
Low & Bonar on Monday said Nuway, which makes high traffic entrance matting for airports, hotels and hospitals, would complement its business in manufacturing textile entrance matting systems.
The shares have also been subjected to buying from its own directors, according to a firm tracking UK corporate directors share dealings.
Directus, a department of Edinburgh Financial publishing, said four Low & Bonar directors snapped up a total of 79,500 shares at 207p to 210p each in July.
